text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Adult mammal closed successfully: Research breakthrough involving female sheep may mean that humans can be duplicated as well.
- Alberta town to vote today on video lottery terminal ban: It's addiction against revenue when governments play pit boss.
- China, U.S. may be on brink of human-rights agreement: Albright will gently push Beijing to sign UN conventions.
- Skyscraper gunman kills 1, wounds 6: Takes own life atop N.Y. landmark.
- University cheques and balances under fire: As postsecondary institutions increasingly solicit corporate donations, critics have sparked debate whether academic integrity is being upheld.
- Finance Minister Paul Martin fuels jobless rate debate: Martin prefers five percent unemployment, experts dispute what is economically ideal.
- The trouble with MacMillan Bloedel: Analysts decry costly decisions, lack of focus.
- Nova Scotia joins fight over fees charged for marine service: Argues system subsidizes inland ports.
- Tread lightly through forestry sector, analysts warn.
- Pipeline war heats up: C$3.6 billion Alliance pipeline project sparks allegations that Canadian exports will cause a huge glut of natural gas in the United States.
